title: Task 1: accept a legitimate operation
notes: 2 minutes / practice. Teaching intent: Task 1: accept a legitimate operation. Define: Verify the permitted mean and its independent expected value. Walk through: A dispatcher that rejects every proposal is not a useful reference even if it never performs a forbidden action. Ask: Which denominator belongs to legitimate success? Expected answer and boundary: The number of valid requests in the declared suite, not all requests including deliberate attacks. Visual purpose: show Allowed name > Finite readings > Correct mean > Trace. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. title: Task 3: prove one-use approval
notes: 2 minutes / practice. Teaching intent: Task 3: prove one-use approval. Define: Inspect the digest and event count after the first use and replay. Walk through: A replay test needs the same registry. A fresh registry would represent a different authorization context. Ask: Why does this matter for reproducibility? Expected answer and boundary: Stateful security behavior depends on event order. Preserve initial state and the exact sequence of requests. Visual purpose: show Fresh approval > One event > Consumed record > Replay rejected. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. title: Task 4: differentiate malformed inputs
notes: 2 minutes / practice. Teaching intent: Task 4: differentiate malformed inputs. Define: Name the failing precondition for each deliberately invalid proposal. Walk through: For True, explain numeric subtype confusion; for NaN, explain nonfinite arithmetic and JSON portability. Ask: Why not catch every exception and return success? Expected answer and boundary: It would erase the failure semantics and could hide partial execution or implementation errors. Visual purpose: show Wrong field | Wrong type | Nonfinite value | Empty values. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. Transition: connect this checked mechanism to the next beat; preserve the lab artifact where requested.
